first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because my mother keeps sending me Santorini photographs. The first screen is calm. It talks about guest numbers and the view, not deals. In the second takeaway it says plainly that most cliff-top spaces hold 15 to 60, and that's why she kept reading. Her summary: Grand Ambassador goes to 250 outdoors, a Canaves Epitome buyout to 170, Canaves and Katikies publish buyouts or take-overs, Le Ciel has its own security, and nothing on the island reaches 400. I read the exclusive-use paragraph and the Canaves entry myself.

journey.quote: The right one depends on how many guests you are inviting, the ceremony you want and the view you want behind you as you say your vows.
journey.reaction: Guest numbers come first. Good. It isn't selling me a sunset in the first line.

journey.quote: Most cliff-top ceremony spaces hold between 15 and 60 guests, so a larger guest list points to a full-property buyout, a winery terrace or the open-air space at Grand Ambassador in Akrotiri.
journey.reaction: Honest, and it saves my assistant an afternoon. It also tells me Santorini is tight for a family our size.

journey.quote: For every other venue, ask whether the wedding spaces, or the whole property, can be closed to other guests.
journey.reaction: That is my first question, asked properly. They understand that a private terrace and a closed hotel are not the same thing.

journey.quote: For a larger guest list, the published options are Grand Ambassador, with outdoor space for up to 250 guests, Venetsanos Winery's Upper Terrace for about 100 seated or 160 standing, and a full buyout of Canaves Epitome for up to 170 guests.
journey.reaction: Clear figures, said without excitement. But 250 is the ceiling, and our list starts at 200. On this island we would have to split the family across properties, and that is where things leak.

journey.section: Caldera terrace, hotel, winery or private venue
journey.quote: If a venue offers its own wedding package, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how to compare it with booking the venue on its own terms.
journey.reaction: A packages link right while I'm deciding what kind of place I want. This is where I feel filed with everyone else.

journey.section: Canaves Oia (Oia Suites, Sunday and Epitome)
journey.quote: **Standout:** With a full buyout, every space at the hotel becomes part of the wedding.
journey.reaction: This is what I want to read. Three hotels with buyouts in one village could become one private wedding, if they sit close enough together.

journey.quote: **Standout:** The hotel is home to Lycabettus Restaurant, which it describes as Greece's only restaurant with two Michelin stars, and the Mare Sanus Spa.
journey.reaction: That kitchen matters for a family dinner the night before. But 39 suites is a pre-wedding dinner, not the wedding.

journey.quote: Children above 13 are welcome, and younger children are pointed to the group's hotel in Fira.
journey.reaction: Useful to know early. Our nieces and nephews are small and they stay with the family. That rules Katikies out for us.

journey.quote: Imerovigli holds five venues on this list, all small, from a hotel with a private villa for vows to a resort with 17 rooms.
journey.reaction: Said plainly. My assistant skips this whole section, which is exactly what the sentence lets her do.

journey.quote: It hosts proposals, weddings, honeymoons and anniversaries, and offers wedding and honeymoon packages.
journey.reaction: The one venue that fits my numbers, and the first thing I learn is that it sells packages and proposals. It makes the largest option sound like the most standard one.

journey.quote: **Standout:** Easy access from the road, very few steps and wheelchair ramps, and a team of more than 30, including a DJ and security.
journey.reaction: Security, and step-free access for my grandmother. It's the first time the page mentions security at all. My question is whether our own team could work with theirs.

journey.section: Getting to Santorini for your wedding
journey.quote: [Santorini Airport (JTR)](https://www.jtr-airport.gr/en) is served by Aegean Airlines, Olympic Air and Sky Express, along with European and Gulf carriers including British Airways, Lufthansa, Qatar Airways, Etihad Airways, Gulf Air and FlyDubai.
journey.reaction: Gulf carriers and British Airways. Family from Dubai and London is covered, so someone thought beyond Sydney.

journey.section: Getting to Santorini for your wedding
journey.quote: Smartraveller says to expect high temperatures and crowds at popular seaports from May to October, and to carry luggage up and down stairs on most ferries.
journey.reaction: Carrying our own luggage up ferry stairs. My guests won't be on a public ferry. My assistant would cut this from her summary.

journey.quote: Agree a covered or indoor fallback with your venue in advance.
journey.reaction: Wildfire and earthquakes are covered calmly, with a plan attached. Our head of security would want this section.

journey.quote: The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only ones issued in their own country.
journey.reaction: Our lawyers handle this, and we are not only Australian. Skipped.

journey.quote: 3. **Capacity.** What is the seated and standing capacity of the ceremony space and the reception space, and do the figures match your package?
journey.reaction: A good checklist, then 'your package' again. I don't have a package. I have a guest list and a family.

journey.section: Shortlist your Santorini venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The next step is finding out which of them are free on your date, on your terms.
journey.reaction: 'On your terms' is the right note. Quiet, not eager.

journey.section: Shortlist your Santorini venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: One person throughout is what I want. 'For Australian couples' makes me wonder whether a family split between Dubai, London and Sydney is the client they have in mind.

unanswered_questions: Can the three Canaves hotels in Oia be bought out together for one wedding, and how far apart are they?
Can Grand Ambassador be closed to the public for three days for 200 to 400 guests, and how many rooms does it have?
Can a ceremony at one caldera property and a reception at another be run privately for several hundred guests?
Can our own security team work with the venue's, and how are staff phones and guest photography controlled?
Which of these kitchens can cater halal, and can they host family customs across several days?
Have they delivered a wedding of 200 to 400 guests on Santorini, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: It hosts proposals, weddings, honeymoons and anniversaries, and offers wedding and honeymoon packages.
turn_offs_found.why: This is the only venue on the page that reaches my numbers, and the copy introduces it through its packages and proposal offers. It puts the one large option in the standard-client bracket, and being treated as a standard client is one of my main fears.

turn_offs_found.quote: If a venue offers its own wedding package, our guide to [Greece wedding packages](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages) sets out how to compare it with booking the venue on its own terms.
turn_offs_found.why: It comes right while I'm choosing the kind of place I want, and it makes packages sound like the normal way to compare. Together with 'your package' in checklist item 3 and the 'Packages' item 11, the page keeps assuming I am buying a bundle.

turn_offs_found.quote: Smartraveller says to expect high temperatures and crowds at popular seaports from May to October, and to carry luggage up and down stairs on most ferries.
turn_offs_found.why: With the public bus and taxis line before it, the arrival section is pitched at an ordinary holidaymaker. It tells me how to carry my own bags, when what I'm judging is whether a planner understands guests who don't.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Canaves about a combined buyout of its three Oia hotels and Grand Ambassador about full closure and room count
Our head of security, for the Le Ciel security line and the wildfire and earthquake section
My mother, for the Canaves buyouts and the Andronis restaurant for a family dinner

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Santorini venues through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet, with no bargain talk, and I prefer that. But I don't fill in web forms, Santorini only just reaches our numbers, and the page keeps returning to packages. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Take the package tilt out: drop 'and offers wedding and honeymoon packages' from the Grand Ambassador intro (or move it below the capacity line), remove the Greece packages link from 'Caldera terrace, hotel, winery or private venue', and reword checklist item 3 ('do the figures match your package?') to 'do the figures match your guest list?'.

Trim the public-transport framing in 'Getting to Santorini': cut 'a public bus and taxis' and the ferry luggage-on-stairs line, and keep the Gulf and European carriers, which already speak to guests flying from Dubai and London.
Soften 'quotes in AUD for Australian couples' in the closing section so a family spread across several countries doesn't read itself out of the brief.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, closure, security, discretion and family customs)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why

Title, deferred business details (fees, private logistics, security, scale proof, who is on the ground, call first) and absent prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing or 'not published' explanations

assumptions: Layla is considering Santorini for a 200 to 400 guest wedding; the persona card doesn't name a destination.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
Her family includes young children, an older relative and needs halal catering; this fits the card's 'family customs' and 'catering' trust signals, but the card doesn't state it.
